transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-24
Start time (UTC): 15:00
Duration: 19 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Lena Park (Vistron Head of ML), Tom Reilly (Vistron Platform Eng), Anika Singh (Vistron Security)

Auto-summary: quick status + bench review, gating for gateway greenlight, confirm KMS and SAML, plan extended bench

Topics: Environment access, latency benchmarks, KMS and SSO, fallback

Action items: see metadata

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Okay great, let's get started. Thanks everyone for jumping on. Quick agenda: access & greenlight, bench results, security handoff. We have 19 minutes. Uh, Lena you said you had the p99 numbers uploaded?
[00:18] Lena Park: Yeah I, I put the spreadsheet in the drive, sorry it's in the folder named 'march-run' — I think Diego had a quick glance. The p50 is around 70 ms, p95 about 210, and p99 is spiking at 540 on the staging gateway under the 1x token profile.
[00:34] Diego Alvarez: Mm-hmm, yeah that's what I saw. There's a tail when we hit bursts — looks like prefix cache miss and the KV cash — K V cash — sorry — the K-V cache warmup is the culprit. If we prime the cache it drops to ~320 for p99.
[00:54] Tom Reilly: Right, so that suggests we need either a warmup step before the canary, or we accept a higher p99 initially. For production we really want sub-400 consistently. Cost tradeoff here, right? Do we bump up to ded— Redwood Dedicate GPUs for lower latency?
[01:12] Maya Chen: Yeah, so two levers: dedicated capacity (reserved) decreases tail, also quant and batching profile; Diego's suggested q4 quant profile plus continuous batching keeps throughput high. But dedicated is costlier. We discussed this in the SSO call last week.
[01:32] Anika Singh: On security, we still need the KMS workflow. We're using our cloud KMS, we want customer-managed keys. Do you support HSM-backed keys and envelope encryption? Also need audit logs export to our SIEM — we require at least 90 days of queryable logs.
[01:50] Diego Alvarez: We support KMS integration and can use customer-managed keys. HSM is supported via our KMS connector but we'll need the key ARN and admin access to set up the service role. Logs: we can push audit logs to S3 and you can pick them up for SIEM, or we can enable syslog forwarding to a collector.
[02:10] Lena Park: Is that documented somewhere? The security docs that show the IAM role and the exact log fields.
[02:16] Maya Chen: Yes, I'll send the security whitepaper and the SAML/KMS runbook. Action: Maya to share security docs.
[02:22] [crosstalk]
[02:24] Tom Reilly: Quick question on SAML: we run Okta. How granular is RBAC? Can we map roles down to per-environment? We don't want dev traffic hitting the staging gateway.
[02:38] Diego Alvarez: We support SCIM + SAML, role mapping per team, and environment-level RBAC. Small caveat — currently the console labels environments as 'prod/stage/dev' strings; if you need a separate VPC access rule we can gate by project tag.
[02:56] Anika Singh: Also need to confirm if data at rest encryption uses your keys or ours. We can't have plaintext logs stored on your side.
[03:06] Diego Alvarez: We do server-side encryption, and with customer KMS keys we can ensure we never hold the unwrapped data. There's also options for zero-knowledge logging where only hashes are sent if that helps (less useful for debugging though).
[03:22] Maya Chen: Back to bench results — Diego, can you explain the two runs you did and the differences?
[03:27] Diego Alvarez: Sure. Run A was 1x token profile, sequential requests, cold cache. Run B added a short 5-minute priming load to warm KV cache and used the continuous batching with 8-request windows. Run B p99 dropped from ~540 to ~320 and token throughput increased ~18%.
[03:47] Lena Park: That's encouraging. Our SLA target is p99 < 400 for the user facing flow. So if we do a priming procedure before canary and enable the continuous batch settings, we should meet it.
[03:58] Tom Reilly: How deterministic is that? If we have spikes will p99 blow up again?
[04:05] Diego Alvarez: Spikes can reintroduce cold paths if the prefix isn't in cache. We recommend two mitigations: prefix caching on the client side and short-lived warmers that run at low qps during off-hours. Also route-based warmups for new prompts.
[04:20] Maya Chen: Also, there's smart routing. If a high-priority endpoint needs to be low-latency, we can pin it to dedicated instances and route lower-priority traffic to shared hosted endpoints. That gives you SLO guarantees for critical APIs.
[04:34] Anika Singh: On the compliance side, we need SOC2 Type II evidence and your incident response playbook. We're preparing for an internal audit early Q2.
[04:44] Maya Chen: Yes, we have SOC 2 reports and IR playbook — will share under NDA. I'll attach the security pack to the SOW email.
[04:52] [08:30] Lena Park: Quick nit — Diego's run used a quantized model variant Q4_8bit; we need to double-check quality on our eval set. If quant causes hallucination regressions, we can't deploy that variant.
[08:46] Diego Alvarez: Right, we flagged that. We have a quality monitor; the Redwood eval harness will run your prompt set and produce delta metrics. If delta > threshold we won't recommend that quant profile.
[08:58] Tom Reilly: Perfect. On networking you said we need an egress rule for health checks — what's the IP range?
[09:06] Diego Alvarez: We'll provide a CIDR list. For private deployments it's peered; for hosted we provide NAT egress ranges — I'll include them in the gating doc.
[09:20] Maya Chen: Let's go through the gating checklist. Items: SAML configured, KMS key provided, gateway creds provisioned, bench p99 under 400 after warmup, rollback policy agreed. Anyone want to add?
[09:36] Anika Singh: Add: audit log delivery verified to SIEM and retention policy confirmed.
[09:42] Lena Park: And QA signoff on model quality after quant profile.
[09:48] Maya Chen: Great. So next steps — we'll get SOW + security docs to you by Thursday. SE will run the extended bench with your eval prompts. Customer to provision KMS test key and SAML group by Friday. We'll reconvene in a week unless blockers.
[10:05] Tom Reilly: One more thing — pricing: we need the breakout of dedicated vs hosted pricing and an estimate for the canary month.
[10:13] Maya Chen: I'll include a pricing worksheet in the SOW. It will show committed reserved cost vs on-demand hosted rates and an estimate for expected token throughput. Also include expected savings from batching and caching.
[10:25] Lena Park: Sounds good. Any concerns about data residency? Our European users must have data kept in EU for legal reasons.
[10:33] Diego Alvarez: We can route EU traffic to the EU region; for private deployments we can deploy entirely in your EU VPC. We'll note that in the SOW options.
[10:44] Anika Singh: Can we get a short runbook for incident escalation — who to call at 2am?
[10:51] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll include on-call contact and escalation matrix in the playbook.
[10:56] [crosstalk]
[11:00] Maya Chen: OK, to summarize the concrete actions: SOW + security docs by 2026-03-26, KMS key and SAML group from Vistron by 2026-03-29, SE bench run and upload by 2026-03-30. Diego will share the bench artifact and a short README of the warmup strategy.
[11:20] Lena Park: Good. That timeline should work.
[11:24] Tom Reilly: We'll try to get KMS key earlier if possible.
[11:27] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll reconvene next Tuesday same time unless we hit blockers. Bye.
[11:33] End of call.

Notes about transcription: some product names were auto-corrected; 'KV cache' shows up as 'K V cash' in places. Also 'Redwood Dedicated' may be seen as 'Redwood Dedicate'.
